sources: HPC 2020 Annual Report (Hebrew) section on Kishon East; Port2Port 29.11.2020 news
notes: Kishon East basin returned to HPC and reopened for operations in Q4 2020 after infrastructure works:contentReference[oaicite:109]{index=109}. Cost included in 2020 PPE additions (no standalone figure).

project_name_short: Structural rehabilitation of Kishon West pier
amount_status: Estimated HPC share of total project cost
sources: IPC 2022 Annual Report (Hebrew) p.X; HPC 2024 FS Note 25A
notes: Joint IPC-HPC project to reinforce Kishon West pier (Mar 2021–Dec 2025). Total ~₪64m+VAT; HPC share ~₪25–30m:contentReference[oaicite:110]{index=110}. As of 2024, ~₪3.5m still uncapitalized:contentReference[oaicite:111]{index=111}. Commission upon completion (~Q4 2025).

New mobile harbor crane for Kishon and other heavy gear (for projects completing by mid-2026). Value ₪36.6m; ₪9.7m of this was not on books as of 31/12/2024:contentReference[oaicite:112]{index=112}. Deliveries 2023–2026.

amount_status: No standalone cost disclosed (part of multi-year capex program)
sources: HPC Q3 2022 Interim Rep – Note on crane projects
notes: Multi-year crane program: purchase of 5 new STS for Kishon and heightening/extension of 4 RTGs at Carmel. Noted in 2022 after supplier insolvency; project continued under administrator:contentReference[oaicite:113]{index=113}. Cost envelope not stated (~could be >₪100m). Commissioning expected 2022–2024 (phased). Included as major capacity upgrade event.

column22: After structural faults found in main terminal, a temporary facility was set up nearby in 2022. Estimated cost ~₪7–8.8m:contentReference[oaicite:114]{index=114}:contentReference[oaicite:115]{index=115} as operating expense (equipment rental), not capitalized. Included here for record, but **excluded from K stock**.

project_name_short: Transfer of Marine Dept to IPC
relevant_for_K_B: Sale price (approx); book value of disposed assets TBD
notes: HPC 2020 Annual Report – IPC agreement; HPC 2024 FS Note 1B
column22: Sale of all pilotage/towage operations and assets to IPC, effective Nov 3 2020. IPC paid ~₪180m:contentReference[oaicite:116]{index=116}. Represents a one-time **removal** of HPC capital (tugboats, etc.). For K series, use the assets’ book value (not the payment) once known.

project_name_short: Waterfront redevelopment: land swap & new port infrastructure
amount_status: Max compensation agreed; actual use in assets ~₪115m so far
sources: Haifa Port privatization roadshow (2020); HPC 2024 FS pp.55-56
notes: City waterfront plan: ~56 dunam port land removed for urban use. HPC to get ₪150m and alternate land to relocate port ops:contentReference[oaicite:117]{index=117}. By 2024, ₪115m received; used ~₪19.9m for investment property, ~₪77.6m for new equipment/yard, ~₪7m expenses:contentReference[oaicite:118]{index=118}. New facilities being developed 2022–25. Only the new port infrastructure counts toward K (land reclassified out).

amount_status: Approx. HPC share; IPC spent ~₪1.8b on infra
notes: Major expansion: 700m quay, 16m depth, 273 dunam yard:contentReference[oaicite:121]{index=121}. Opened Oct 2010. IPC built civil works (~₪1.8b):contentReference[oaicite:122]{index=122}, HPC invested in 6 new STS and 12 RTG cranes plus systems (est. ~₪200–250m). Hugely increased Haifa’s container capacity (doubling throughput):contentReference[oaicite:123]{index=123}.
Ordered ~2009, delivered 2011: a new powerful escort tug (Ilan 1) for Haifa Port. Cost ~₪45m. Improved capability to berth large vessels. Asset transferred to IPC in 2020 Sea Dept sale.

Second new-generation tug acquired by HPC. Arrived Nov 2015:contentReference[oaicite:127]{index=127}, cost ~₪43m. Augmented Haifa’s fleet for mega-ships (2M alliance):contentReference[oaicite:128]{index=128}. Like Ilan1, left HPC in 2020 sale.

Purchase of 5 modern mobile harbor cranes for Kishon West, as part of competition preparations. First 2 arrived Sept 2023, next 3 due mid-2024:contentReference[oaicite:131]{index=131}:contentReference[oaicite:132]{index=132}. Project ~₪100m. Enables efficient bulk/general cargo ops on renovated pier. (Post-privatization investment, initiated by HPC earlier.)
